title: Erdős 105 in Higher Dimensions
description: Higher-dimensional analogue of Erdős Problem #105: does the threshold phenomenon for rich 2-flats avoiding obstacles persist in R^d for d ≥ 3?

meta.author: Open problem (formalized in Lean 4)
originalContributions: Formalization of higher-dimensional Erdős-Purdy problem statement in Lean 4
Definition of 2-flats, rich 2-flats, and unblocked 2-flats in R^d
Survey of known results and infrastructure requirements
meta.assumptions: No axioms. Problem statement only (the answer is unknown).

overview.historicalContext: Erdős Problem #105 asks about lines in R². The d=2 case has a known threshold Θ(n) for obstacles (Beck-Szemerédi-Trotter). The higher-dimensional generalization to 2-flats in R^d is open.
overview.problemStatement: For d ≥ 3: given n points A in R^d (not all in one 2-flat) and cn obstacle points B, must there exist a 2-flat containing ≥2 points of A and avoiding all of B?
overview.text: Higher-dimensional analogue of Erdős 105: rich 2-flats avoiding obstacles in R^d
overview.proofStrategy: Problem statement only. Three possible approaches identified: direct generalization via incidence bounds, counterexample hunting in R^3, or reduction to d=2 via projection.
keyInsights: Szemerédi-Trotter is specific to d=2 (points and lines). For d≥3, polynomial partitioning (Guth-Katz) is the relevant tool.
The answer may differ from d=2: higher dimensions have more 2-flats per point, which could make blocking harder or easier depending on the geometry.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.summary: Definitions of PointD, TwoFlat, rich, unblocked, and not-coplanar conditions in R^d.
sections.mathContext: Generalizes the d=2 definitions (Point, Line) from Erdos105Problem.lean to arbitrary dimension.

sections.title: Open Problem Statement
sections.summary: The conjecture: ∃ c > 0 such that cn obstacles cannot block all rich 2-flats. Survey of known results and infrastructure needs.
sections.mathContext: Connects to Beck-Szemerédi-Trotter (d=2) and Guth-Katz (polynomial partitioning for d≥3).

crossReferences.description: Generalizes the d=2 Erdős-Purdy problem (lines in R²) to d≥3 (2-flats in R^d).

conclusion.summary: Formalization of the open problem statement for Erdős 105 in R^d. No theorems proved (the answer is unknown). Defines 2-flats, rich/unblocked conditions, and the conjecture in Lean 4.
conclusion.implications: Progress would require incidence bounds for 2-flats in R^d, which are not yet in Mathlib. The Guth-Katz polynomial partitioning framework is the most promising approach.
openQuestions: Does the threshold exist for d=3?
Can counterexamples be found computationally for small n in R^3?
